newsitem.title: CHINA: China to expand sweep for fake goods.
newsitem.headline: China to expand sweep for fake goods.

text.p: China will begin inspections of medium-sized department stores in a drive to crack down on fake or shoddy goods, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

The State Bureau of Technical Supervision and the Ministry of Internal Trade would begin quality checks of products at stores with annual sales of more than 50 million yuan ($6.0 million), the newspaper said.

Authorities had already carried out checks of state-owned department stores and other shopping centres with sales volumes of at least 100 million yuan ($12 million) a year, it quoted Ye Bolin, a quality inspection official under the technical supervision bureau, as saying.

"The move has helped strengthen management of markets, improve the quality of commodities and...protect the legal rights of the consumers," the newspaper quoted Wang Qing, an official with the Ministry of Internal Trade, as saying.
Quality checks in 54 large department stores in Beijing had indicated gaps in business management and a low production level in China, Ye said without elaborating.
